name: Zoom Communications, Inc.

profile.description: Zoom Communications positions itself as an 'AI-first, open work platform built for human connection,' spanning Meetings, Zoom Phone, Contact Center and the broader AI-first Customer Experience (CX) portfolio, Team Chat, Docs, Workvivo and AI Companion. Fiscal Q2 2027 (quarter ended July 31, 2026) revenue was $1,277.2M (+4.9% YoY), with Enterprise revenue up 7.8% — its fastest in three years — while Online revenue grew just 0.6%. Management raised FY2027 guidance to $5.085-$5.095B of revenue, $6.08-$6.12 of non-GAAP EPS and $1.78-$1.82B of free cash flow. Founded by CEO Eric Yuan in 2011 and headquartered in San Jose, Zoom holds a strategic investment portfolio that grew to $3.79B and carries essentially no debt.

innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Zoom has turned a single-product video app into a multi-product platform — Phone, Contact Center, Virtual Agent, Workvivo, Docs and AI Companion — and the Enterprise segment now delivers 62% of revenue ($787.5M, +7.8% YoY) [1]; this is a significant new revenue stream, but Online (+0.6%) shows the original franchise is ex-growth, so it falls short of a transformative 3. AI Deployment (2/2): AI products are shipping with measurable traction — Zoom Virtual Agent customers rose 256% YoY and the AI-first CX portfolio delivered 'high-double-digit ARR expansion' in Q2 FY2027 [1]; AI Companion 3.0 added agentic reasoning, memory and task-action capabilities [3]. Market Share (1/2): Zoom remains a top video-meetings brand with 4,625 customers above $100K TTM revenue (+8.2%), but Enterprise net dollar expansion of 99% indicates stable, not gaining, share against bundled Microsoft Teams and Google Meet [1]. Pipeline (1/2): Management describes moving customers 'from conversation to completion' as a 'system of action,' yet no specific next-generation products with launch dates and revenue targets were disclosed [1]. R&D Intensity (1/1): R&D was $242.5M in Q2 (19% of revenue) and 18.1% TTM, in line with application-software peers [2].
innovation.label: STRONG

inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): Zoom's purpose of building a platform 'for human connection' is reinforced by Eric Yuan's long-running 'deliver happiness' philosophy that puts employee happiness ahead of customer happiness, a specific and personally rooted culture thesis [3]; it has not been validated over decades, so it stops at 3. Community Impact (2/2): Zoom Cares has funded $35M of monetary grants, $25M of product grants and $4M of employee-led giving since inception, with the 2022 report alone citing $30.9M of grants and in-kind donations focused on education, social equity, climate and youth mental health [5]. Employee Retention (0/2): No turnover or tenure data was found after searching. Insider Buying (0/2): FMP shows zero open-market purchases and 23-53 open-market sales in each of the last four quarters (e.g., 34 sales in Q3 2026 and 23 in Q4 2026 to date) — persistent net selling [6].
inspiration.label: DEVELOPING

infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored as a Growth stock (raw 7.99/10, rounds to 8). Debt-to-equity of 0.5% [2], ROE of 32.3% (2x weight) [2], net margin of 65.2% [2] — heavily inflated by $1.61B of Q2 gains on strategic investments, though even the 24.6% GAAP operating margin would clear the 20% target [1] — and a forward P/E of ~15.7 (derived: $95.50 price over the $6.10 midpoint of FY2027 non-GAAP EPS guidance) [1][2] all score 1.0. The 5yr revenue CAGR of 12.9% (FY2021 $2.65B to FY2026 $4.87B) also scores 1.0 at 2x weight, though nearly all of it came in the pandemic surge and FY2024-FY2026 growth ran only 3-4% [2]. Revenue growth of 4.9% YoY scores 0.83, and FMP's forward PEG of 2.84 scores just 0.08 at 2x weight, reflecting low expected earnings growth [1][2]. Liquidity is far above the floor at ~$284M of average daily turnover (2.97M shares x $95.50).
infrastructure.label: STRONG

ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (5/9): Zoom's core meetings franchise is exposed — Online revenue grew only 0.6% YoY and Enterprise net dollar expansion sits at 99% [1], while Microsoft and Google bundle AI assistants into Teams and Meet and cross-platform AI notetakers reduce the stickiness of any single meeting tool; AI agents completing work asynchronously could also reduce meeting volume over time. Protection comes from Zoom's installed base, its contact-center and telephony workloads that carry regulatory and integration switching costs, and the fact that real-time human video remains a substrate that AI agents augment rather than eliminate. AI Opportunity (1/1): Zoom is generating AI revenue — its AI-first CX portfolio delivered high-double-digit ARR growth and Zoom Virtual Agent customers grew 256% YoY in Q2 FY2027 [1].
ai_resilience.label: MODERATE

infinite_game.summary: Through Sinek's lens Zoom is a mixed player: Eric Yuan's 'deliver happiness' cause and founder continuity give it a genuine purpose, and the company has adapted from a video app into an AI-first CX and work platform. But its competitive language is about differentiation in a crowded market, its capital allocation leans on large buybacks, and its 2023 layoffs dented the Circle of Safety Yuan preaches.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): 'Human connection' and 'deliver happiness' form a distinctive, service-oriented cause tied directly to the founder's story and visible in decisions such as free service to schools during COVID [3][5]. It is genuine and referenced by leadership, but it has existed for barely a decade and has not been tested through a leadership transition.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Founder-CEO continuity since 2011 and an explicit employee-first culture thesis support trust [3]. Offsetting that, no current retention data is available, and insiders sell stock every quarter with no open-market purchases [6], so we score adequate rather than exceptional trust.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (1/1): Zoom frames its strategy as being 'open' and as a 'system of action for modern work' that interoperates across ecosystems rather than trying to destroy Teams or Google Meet [1][3]; Microsoft's bundling has pushed Zoom to improve by building Phone, Contact Center and agentic AI rather than fighting a pure price war.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): The 2024 rebrand from Zoom Video to Zoom Communications and the build-out of CX, Phone and AI Companion show real adaptation, with Enterprise now 62% of revenue [1]. Video meetings remain the core and the Online business is shrinking in relative terms, so this is an extension rather than a full reinvention.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Zoom has spent ~18% of revenue on R&D while growth slowed to ~4-5% [2] and committed $295.4M of new strategic investments in one quarter to position for the AI era [1]. Against this, it repurchased 3.7M shares for $360.5M in the same quarter and leans on buybacks to support per-share results, a finite-game habit [1].

investment_thesis: Zoom is a cash machine priced like a value stock: FY2027 guidance calls for $1.78-$1.82B of free cash flow on ~$5.09B of revenue and $6.08-$6.12 of non-GAAP EPS, putting the shares at roughly 15.7x forward earnings with essentially no debt and a $3.79B strategic-investment portfolio that produced $1.61B of gains in Q2 alone [1][2]. Growth is quietly improving where it matters — Enterprise revenue rose 7.8%, its best rate in three years, customers above $100K grew 8.2% to 4,625, and the AI-first CX portfolio is compounding at high-double-digit ARR rates with Zoom Virtual Agent customers up 256% [1]. Management raised full-year guidance and continues to retire shares (3.7M repurchased in Q2, ~$1.3B authorization remaining) [1].
thesis_continued: The bear case is that Zoom is a mature, ex-growth franchise whose headline profits flatter reality. Total revenue is growing under 5%, Online revenue just 0.6%, and Enterprise net dollar expansion of 99% means existing customers are not expanding [1]. GAAP net income of $1.54B in Q2 came overwhelmingly from investment gains, so the 65% TTM net margin and single-digit trailing P/E are not repeatable [1][2]. FMP's forward PEG of 2.84 signals little earnings growth, stock-based compensation still runs ~14.6% of revenue, and Microsoft and Google bundle AI-enabled meetings for free inside their suites [2]. Insiders have sold in every recent quarter with no open-market purchases [6], and the Inspire Impact Score of -49 (MISALIGNED, Abortion Activism) limits suitability for faith-based mandates.
key_catalysts: Fiscal Q3 2027 results (late November 2026) against guidance of $1.275-$1.280B revenue and $1.46-$1.48 non-GAAP EPS — another Enterprise acceleration would support a re-rating from ~15.7x forward earnings [1]
Scaling of the AI-first CX portfolio (Contact Center, Zoom Virtual Agent) after high-double-digit ARR growth and 256% Virtual Agent customer growth in Q2 FY2027 [1]
Capital return and monetization of the $3.79B strategic-investment portfolio, with ~$1.3B of buyback authorization remaining and $1.78-$1.82B of FY2027 FCF guided [1]
key_risks: Core meetings stagnation: Online revenue +0.6% YoY and Enterprise net dollar expansion of 99% show limited expansion within the installed base as Microsoft Teams and Google Meet bundle AI features [1]
Earnings-quality risk: $1.61B of Q2 investment gains drove GAAP EPS of $5.15 versus $1.55 non-GAAP — mark-downs in the strategic portfolio could produce equally large GAAP losses [1]
Persistent insider selling (23-53 open-market sales per quarter, no purchases) and stock-based compensation near 14.6% of revenue dilute the per-share benefit of buybacks [2][6]
